html:
On 1 January 1863 President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, declaring free all enslaved people in the states then in rebellion against the Union. It applied to over three million people.

It did not free those in loyal border states, and it could only take effect where Union armies advanced. But it made the Civil War a war to end slavery, kept Britain and France from backing the South, and allowed Black men to enlist. About 180,000 served in the Union army.

Slavery was abolished everywhere in the United States by the Thirteenth Amendment in December 1865. Juneteenth, 19 June, marks the day in 1865 when news of freedom was proclaimed in Galveston, Texas. The Reconstruction that followed tried to make freedom real.
